parts.prompt_markdown:
3 students from Greenfield college are selected at random.

Find the probability that none of these 3 students travel to college by car.

11 students from Greenfield college are selected at random.

Find the probability that fewer than 9 of these 11 students travel to college by car or by bus.

skills: model the number of successes with a binomial distribution
use binomial probabilities for small values of n
combine complementary events (none / fewer than)
methods: Binomial distribution with appropriate success probability

questions.stem_markdown: There are a large number of students at Greenfield college. Each student travels to college by car, by bus or on foot, independently of any other student. The probability that any student travels by car is 0.4. The probability that any student travels by bus is 0.35.

questions.stem_markdown:
The Splash Club has 26 members, of whom 16 are swimmers and 10 are divers. No member is both a swimmer and a diver. The club committee consists of 6 of these 26 members.

In how many ways can the club committee be selected if it must include at least 2 swimmers and at least 2 divers?

parts.prompt_markdown: Draw up the probability distribution table for X.

The red spinner, with sides numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, is spun repeatedly.

Find the probability that it lands on 4 for the first time before the 8th spin.

skills: derive the probability distribution of a discrete random variable
calculate variance from the probability distribution
model ‘first success’ timing for a repeated sequence of trials
methods: distribution table using independence and comparison of two spinner outcomes
geometric probability for first landing on 4 before a given spin

questions.stem_markdown:

The random variable X denotes the higher of the two scores obtained. If the two scores are equal, then the value of X is 0.

parts.prompt_markdown: Draw a fully labelled tree diagram to illustrate this information, including all the probabilities.
